chapters.title: Chapter 7: Building and Backtesting a Mean Reversion System

lessons.title: Designing Entry and Exit Rules Around a Z-Score

children.text: A z-score, an RSI reading, a Bollinger Band touch, these have all been signals so far, not systems. A signal tells you something is unusual. A system tells you exactly what to do about it, in advance, before the ambiguity of a live market talks you out of following your own rules. This lesson turns Chapter 2's z-score into a complete, precisely specified entry and exit framework, closing every gap Chapter 3's simplified backtest deliberately left open.

body.text: A complete mean reversion system needs an entry threshold, and three distinct exit rules doing three different jobs: a target exit for when the trade worked, a stop-loss for when it didn't, and a time-based exit, sized off the stock's own half-life, for when it simply isn't resolving either way.

children.text: The Entry Threshold: A Frequency-vs-Strength Trade-off

Lesson 5's statGrid already contains the entire trade-off in three numbers. A looser entry threshold catches more trades, but each one is a weaker, less statistically unusual deviation, closer to ordinary noise. A tighter threshold catches fewer trades, but each one clears a higher bar. There is no universally correct answer, only a choice that should be made deliberately, not by accident.

body.caption: Entry threshold choice: frequency vs strength

cells: More trades, but many are weak, closer to routine noise
A reasonable balance, used throughout Chapters 2 and 3
Fewer opportunities, but each one is a genuinely extreme, higher-conviction deviation
z-score crosses back through a smaller band, e.g. ±0.5, not necessarily all the way to 0
"It worked": the bulk of the reversion has happened, without waiting for the last, lowest-expected-value sliver of the move
A fixed adverse percentage move from entry, e.g. -5%
"It didn't work": cut the loss before a statistical bet turns into an open-ended one
A multiple of the stock's own estimated half-life, e.g. 3 x half-life
"It's taking too long": the statistical basis for holding has likely expired, whatever the price is doing

body.text: Chapter 3's backtest used a flat 10-trading-day time stop for every trade, regardless of the stock. That was a simplification. A stock with a 3-day half-life and a stock with a 12-day half-life do not deserve the same time budget. Sizing the time-based exit as a multiple of Chapter 2's half-life, say 3 times, gives each stock a time stop proportional to its own actual reversion speed instead of one arbitrary number applied to everything.

children.text: On a volatile day, a position can technically satisfy the target and the stop-loss condition within the same session, or a time-based exit can coincide with a target being hit. A system needs a fixed, pre-decided priority order for this, not a judgment call made in the moment. The disciplined choice is to check the stop-loss first. A stop-loss exists precisely to protect capital when a trade is behaving unusually, and a session volatile enough to trigger two exit conditions at once is exactly the kind of unusual behavior a stop-loss is designed to respect, not override.
A Practical Constraint: Shorting Is Not Symmetric in India

markDefs.definition: The NSE mechanism that allows a trader to borrow shares to sell short and carry that position beyond the same trading day, unlike ordinary intraday short selling in the cash market.

children.text: An entry rule that looks symmetric on paper, buy below -2, sell above +2, is not equally easy to execute on both sides in Indian cash equity markets. Most retail brokers only permit short selling in the cash market on an intraday basis, squared off the same day, not carried overnight the way a multi-day reversion trade usually needs. Carrying a short position for several days generally requires either

, available only on a specific list of stocks, or expressing the short view through the futures and options market instead of the cash market. A system's rules should account for this from the start, not discover it only when the first overbought signal fires on a stock with no practical way to act on it.

body.code:
def generate_exit(row, entry_price, entry_zscore, half_life, days_held,
                   target_band=0.5, stop_loss_pct=-0.05, time_stop_multiple=3):
    ret = (row["close"] - entry_price) / entry_price

    hit_stop = ret <= stop_loss_pct
    hit_target = abs(row["zscore"]) <= target_band
    timed_out = days_held >= time_stop_multiple * half_life

    # Stop-loss is checked first: it always takes priority over an
    # ambiguous same-day target or timeout signal.
    if hit_stop:
        return "stop"
    if hit_target:
        return "target"
    if timed_out:
        return "timeout"
    return None
body.caption: A single exit-decision function encoding the fixed priority order: stop-loss first, then target, then a half-life-based time stop.

body.title: Size a half-life-based time stop
body.prompt: A stock's estimated half-life is 6 trading days. Using a time-stop rule of 3 times the half-life, after how many trading days should the position be closed if neither the target nor the stop-loss has fired first?
body.explanation: 3 x 6 = 18 trading days. This scales the time budget to the specific stock's own reversion speed, rather than applying one flat number to every stock regardless of how fast or slow it typically reverts.

body.title: Two exits fire on the same day
body.question: On the same trading day, a position's price both crosses back through the target band and separately triggers the stop-loss threshold. Which exit should the system apply, and why?
options: The target exit, because reaching the target proves the trade ultimately worked
The stop-loss, because a pre-committed risk rule should never be overridden by an ambiguous, possibly coincidental signal on an unusually volatile day
Whichever the code happens to check first in the source file, since it does not matter
Neither, hold the position an extra day to see which signal was the 'real' one
body.explanation: A day volatile enough to trigger both a target and a stop-loss condition is exactly the kind of unusual session a stop-loss exists to respect. Giving the stop-loss fixed priority removes the temptation to rationalize an ambiguous signal in the trade's favor, which is the entire point of deciding the priority order in advance rather than in the moment.

body.title: Entry and Exit Design: Core Terms

cards.definition: An exit triggered once a price's z-score has crossed back through a smaller band around zero, capturing the bulk of a reversion without waiting for the deviation to fully close to zero.
A time-based exit rule set as a multiple of a stock's own estimated half-life, rather than one fixed number of days applied to every stock regardless of its typical reversion speed.
A fixed, pre-decided rule for which exit condition takes precedence when more than one triggers on the same trading day, standardly stop-loss first.
The NSE mechanism allowing a short position to be borrowed and carried beyond a single trading day, required for a multi-day short in the cash market on eligible stocks.

points: The entry threshold is a genuine trade-off between trade frequency and signal strength, not a single correct number. This course has used |z| > 2 as a reasonable default throughout.
A complete system needs three distinct exits: a target exit for when the trade worked, a stop-loss for when it didn't, and a time-based exit for when it simply isn't resolving.
Sizing the time-based exit as a multiple of the stock's own half-life, rather than one flat number for every stock, is a direct, meaningful upgrade over Chapter 3's simplified backtest.
A fixed priority order for exits, standardly stop-loss first, removes the temptation to rationalize an ambiguous signal in the trade's favor on an unusually volatile day.

Short selling in Indian cash equity markets is not symmetric with buying: multi-day shorts generally require Securities Lending and Borrowing or the futures and options market, a practical constraint any system's rules need to account for from the start.
